newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Steel expects to build on strong Q1.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Steel expects to build on strong Q1.

text.p: USX-U.S. Steel Group said Thursday it expects to build on its strong first quarter as the year progresses.

Citing a continued strong market and higher average realized prices, the company recorded first quarter net income of $87 million, or $0.96 per share -- "a substantial improvement over" the $46 million, or $0.49 per share, earned a year earlier.
Revenues were $1.6 billion in both periods.

First quarter operating income was helped by improved average realized prices and product mix compared with last year's first quarter. This improvement was partially offset by higher natural gas costs, the company said.

First quarter operating income was $120 million in 1997, or $42 per ton, on shipments of 2.9 million tons. In first quarter 1996, it recorded operating income of $81 million, or $28 per ton, on shipments of 2.9 million tons.
U.S. Steel "benefited from consistent operating performance, highlighted by record raw steel production during March," USX Corp Chairman Thomas J. Usher said.
"The Steel Group's performance enabled it to take advantage of the ongoing strong market for flat-rolled products and the improving demand for tubular goods."
He said demand is expected to remain high in virtually all of the company's product lines through the second quarter.
"With an ongoing healthy order book and announced price increases in sheet and tubular products, I expect U.S. Steel Group to build on its strong first quarter performance," Usher said.

Late in the first quarter, the company said, the Mon Valley Works near Pittsburgh completed a $15 million upgrade of its Galvalume coating line. This modernization gives the facility the added capability to produce high quality hot-dip galvanized sheet for appliance applications while continuing to produce Galvalume sheet for metal building components.

The largest blast furnace at the Mon Valley Works is scheduled for a reline beginning in June, which will require an outage of about 86 days, U.S. Steel said. No other blast furnace relines are scheduled this year.
